translationRepairs: Xu Jingzong, a native of Xincheng in Hangzhou, was the son of Shanxin, Vice Minister of Rites under the Sui.
Xu Jingzong, a native of Xincheng in Hangzhou, was the son of Xu Shanxin, Vice Minister of Rites under the Sui.
Chinese 善心 is the given name of Xu Jingzong's father; English should identify him as Xu Shanxin rather than bare Shanxin.
In former times, among the attendant ministers of Wu, Yuan Si was not punished for the crime of Liu Pi;
In former times, among the attendant ministers of Wu, Yuan Si (Yuan Ang) was not punished for the crime of Liu Pi;
爰絲 is the historical Yuan Ang (袁盎/爰盎); a brief gloss aids identification without changing the narrative.
Chief Minister Cen Wenti died on campaign, and Jingzong was ordered to serve as acting Vice Director of the Secretariat while keeping his original post.
Zhongshu Ling Cen Wenben died on campaign, and Jingzong was ordered to serve as acting Vice Director of the Secretariat while keeping his original post.
岑文本 is standardly Cen Wenben (Wénběn), not Wenti; 中書令 is Zhongshu Ling.

Jingzong replied, "Emperor Wu sent envoys to open relations with the southwestern tribes, but they were blocked at Dian Lake by the Kunming people. Wishing to attack the state of Kunming, he used the old marshlands of the Hao region to excavate this pool for naval training. This took place in 120 BCE, the third year of Yuanshuo."

Jingzong replied, "Emperor Wu sent envoys to open relations with the southwestern tribes, but they were blocked at Dian Lake by the Kunming people. Wishing to attack the state of Kunming, he used the old marshlands of the Hao region to excavate this pool for naval training. This took place in 120 BCE, the third year of Yuanshou."
Chinese 元狩三年 is Yuanshou 3, not Yuanshuo (元朔); the year 120 BCE is correct for Yuanshou 3.
It was only under Emperor Hui of Han that this city was first built. Afterward Fu Jian, Yao Chang, and the Later Zhou all made it their capital."
It was only under Emperor Hui of Han that this city was first built. Afterward Fu Jian, Yao Chang, and Northern Zhou all made it their capital."
後周 here denotes the Northern Zhou (北周) of the Northern Dynasties, not a generic Later Zhou; clarifying avoids conflation with the Five Dynasties Later Zhou.

Chinese 內史舍人 is the Sui Neishi Sheren; a brief gloss clarifies the office without changing sense.

Earlier, during the Zhenguan era, Emperor Taizong ordered Gao Shilian, Wei Ting, Cen Wenti, Linghu Defen, and other officials, together with scholars versed in distinguished clans from across the realm, to compile the Genealogies of Clans. The work ran to a hundred scrolls, and its rankings were widely judged fair. It was distributed to all prefectures and preserved as a permanent standard.
